business_problem: Seracle needed a more scalable, compliant, and analytics-friendly data platform for its crypto exchange and Web3 infrastructure after self-managing MongoDB Community on DigitalOcean led to manual provisioning, downtime during storage upgrades, and brittle reporting pipelines.
solution_summary: Seracle modernized its crypto-trading and blockchain platform by moving from self-managed MongoDB Community on DigitalOcean to MongoDB Atlas on AWS and replacing external analytics synchronization with MongoDB Charts. Atlas became the primary database for Seracle's exchange software and Web3 infrastructure, giving the team elastic scaling, regional deployment controls, and fewer interruptions when traffic or storage requirements changed. The migration started with a marquee exchange customer and was completed quickly enough to minimize disruption, while Charts removed the need to copy data into Elasticsearch just to build dashboards. Seracle now uses those real-time visualizations internally and exposes them to B2B customers for performance, user, and deal-volume analysis. With Atlas and Charts in one platform, Seracle can onboard higher-volume customers, enforce region-specific data handling, and keep developers focused on shipping features instead of maintaining reporting plumbing.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs Seracle's crypto exchange and Web3 operational database on AWS with managed scalability and regional controls.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Charts
solution_components.role: Provides real-time analytics and dashboards directly from operational MongoDB data without an external sync pipeline.

data_flow: Exchange and Web3 operational data is written into MongoDB Atlas, Atlas serves the live application workloads, and MongoDB Charts reads the same collections directly to power internal and customer-facing dashboards without exporting data to a separate analytics stack.
business_outcome: Seracle raised throughput from hundreds of trades per second to tens of thousands, reduced complexity and downtime, and delivered analytics and compliance capabilities faster and with less developer effort.
metrics: Seracle grew into a USD $100 million business with over 100 staff.
The technical part of the migration was done in less than a week, and the full process took less than two months.
Before Atlas, Seracle could handle 300 to 400 trades per second.
After the move, Seracle can process between 10,000 to 15,000 trades per second.
Building the same data and analytics infrastructure independently would have taken at least 3 years and 40 developers.
architecture_clues: Seracle migrated from MongoDB Community on DigitalOcean to MongoDB Atlas on AWS.
MongoDB Charts replaced a sync-heavy Kibana and Elasticsearch reporting pipeline.
The company uses separate storage locations or clusters to satisfy regional security and compliance requirements.
Dashboards are exposed both internally and to B2B customers on the platform.
